_terms: polaroids.html — what we ask for, what we promise, and how a photo comes down again.
_licence: Photographs here are NOT under the site's CC BY-SA 4.0 licence and carry no onward licence at all. They belong to the people in them and to whoever took them. This is deliberate: CC BY-SA cannot be revoked, so a photo published under it could not be taken back after somebody withdrew consent, and 'it comes down when you say so' would be a promise the licence contradicted. See LICENSE.
_consent: Record only that consent exists and when. Do NOT put anybody's email, message, or contact details in this file — it is a public repository. The conversation stays wherever it happened. To withdraw: delete the entry, delete the file in photos/, and run tools/make-polaroids.py. The wall returns to grey on its own.
_young: Young people who are doing the work and have said yes THEMSELVES are published and credited like anybody else — a lot of Stimpunks volunteers and self-advocates are teenagers, and keeping them off the page hands the credit for their own activities to the adults beside them. The consent has to be theirs: a parent can be in the conversation, but an adult’s yes is not a substitute for the young person’s. Withdrawal works for them exactly as it does for everybody — say so once, and it is deletion. Where somebody is too young to give that consent themselves, we do not publish the photograph and a parent cannot give it for them. Superseded the flat no-children rule on 2026-09-21, Ryan’s call; see DECISIONS.md.
_required: Every photo needs id, alt, subject and consent_on. 'caption' and 'photographer' are optional, but a named photographer must also have given permission — being in a picture is not the same as owning it.
_elsewhere: A photograph may hang somewhere other than Enid's wall. List every other page it appears on in that entry's 'elsewhere' array; make-polaroids.py walks all the HTML and refuses if a page publishes a photo the record does not mention, or if the record names a page that has dropped it. That is what makes withdrawal mean everywhere: delete the entry and the tool refuses to run until the photo is off every page, instead of leaving one behind.

photos.caption: Helen ascends a grand staircase.
photos.subject: Helen Edgar
photos.photographer: a friend who prefers to remain anonymous
photos.note: Helen wrote the description, the caption and the naming; published in her words and not ours. The photographer asked not to be named and gave permission in the same message. The square framing is Helen's own crop, confirmed before publishing — we did not crop it and did not filter it. Also hung in Helen's own room, the Faery Yurt, where she placed it herself in the mockup she sent on 2026-09-20 — with a different description and caption, both also hers, written for that room rather than for the wall.

photos.alt: A white woman with reddish brown hair and brown eyeglasses smiles at the camera with a woodland scene at her back and the sun shining from behind.
photos.caption: Helen in the woods.
photos.subject: Helen Edgar
photos.note: Sent by Helen for both places at once — Enid's wall and her own room, the Faery Yurt, where it is the portrait beside the welcome. The description, the caption and the naming are hers. Not resized, not cropped, and NOT FILTERED: her mockup put a sepia wash over this photograph and polaroids.html promises in as many words that we will not filter anybody, so the wash is the one other thing about her room this site did not carry over. The wooden frame around it is matting and stays.

The old flat no-children rule would have taken her own activity off the page and left the two adults beside her on it; see DECISIONS.md. TWO THINGS TO FIX ON THIS FILE: it is a screenshot of a photo viewer rather than the original, so it carries a caption burnt into the pixels ('Dripping Springs Pride, 2026 / Taken at Pride of Dripping Springs “Pride for All” event a...') that no screen reader can reach, and there is an unrelated person in the background at the left. The clean original should replace it.

photos.alt: Small collage on a lilac and blue marbled ground. A black panel scattered with cartoon eyes holds the words Wish you were here in orange script, red and white stripes, two cut-out figures in straw hats, and a strip reading the national pastime. The word COLONY runs down both sides, and a bee sits in the top corner.
photos.caption: Wish You Were Here
photos.subject: Wish You Were Here, a collage by Isha Snow
photos.note: A PHOTOGRAPH OF A THING AND NOT OF A PERSON: Isha Snow's own collage, photographed by her and sent with her room on 2026-09-29 to hang in the frame she drew for it. The alt text is the frame's own description from her artifact, which she reviewed. Nobody is in the frame; the people in the picture are printed cut-outs that are part of her collage. The background (steps, a garden bed, a wall) was looked at and says nothing about where it was taken. Resized to 1000px on the long edge and saved with no metadata. The file is not cropped; where her frame is shaped differently from the photograph (the round one, the landscape one) the frame shows its middle, which is the collage, and trims the ground around it. Like every photograph here it is outside the site's CC BY-SA licence, and it comes down when she says so.
